Requested Service/CPT: Lower back disc surgery / decompression, CPT 63030
Treating Surgeon: Dr. Okafor, MD, Orthopedic Surgery

To the Appeals & Grievances Department:

I am writing to appeal the denial of prior authorization for CPT 63030 (lumbar disc surgery/decompression), as stated in your Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-01. The stated reason for denial was: "the clinical records submitted do not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment prior to the requested surgery." I disagree with this determination, and I am submitting this appeal within the 180-day window stated in your notice (by 2027-01-28).

**Policy applied to this request**

Harvard Pilgrim delegates prior authorization review for spine surgery to Evolent (formerly National Imaging Associates). I understand that the relevant medical-necessity criteria are contained in Evolent Clinical Guideline 1766 for Lumbar Spine Surgery, part of the "2026 Evolent Clinical Guidelines for Medical Necessity Review – Musculoskeletal Surgery Guidelines," implementation period July 1, 2026 – July 1, 2027. I am relying on the text of that document as retrieved from Evolent's/radmd's published guideline PDF. If a different or more specific version of the criteria was actually used to review my case, I am formally requesting that Harvard Pilgrim/Evolent provide me and Dr. Okafor with the exact version and section applied, as I am entitled to under the plan's clinical review criteria policy.

**Why the clinical record supports medical necessity under this guideline**

The guideline states, for Lumbar Decompression (Laminectomy, Laminotomy, Facetectomy, and Foraminotomy):

"Surgical Indications ● When ALL of the following are present: ○ Neurogenic claudication, and/or radicular leg pain that impairs daily activities ○ Failure of conservative treatment* for a minimum of six (6) weeks within the last six (6) months; NOTE - Failure of conservative treatment is defined as one of the following: ■ Lack of meaningful improvement after a full course of treatment; OR ■ Progression or worsening of symptoms during treatment; OR ■ Documentation of a medical reason the member is unable to participate in treatment... ○ Imaging studies demonstrating moderate to severe stenosis consistent with clinical signs/symptoms."

The guideline also states, for Lumbar Discectomy/Microdiscectomy:

"When ALL of the following are present: ○ Primary radicular symptoms noted upon clinical exam that significantly hinders daily activities ○ Failure of conservative treatment* for a minimum of six (6) weeks within the last six (6) months [same failure definition] ○ Imaging studies showing evidence of inter-vertebral disc herniation that correlate exactly with the individual's symptoms/signs."

My clinical record satisfies each of these elements:

1. **Radicular symptoms/neurogenic claudication impairing daily activities:** I have had 24 months of progressive low back pain, unrelieved by rest, with radicular pain radiating into my right calf, and I am unable to stand for more than 10 minutes at a time. Exam findings include positive provocative testing on the affected side and a neurologic deficit corresponding to the imaged level.

2. **Failure of conservative treatment for a minimum of six weeks within the last six months:** I completed 8 weeks of supervised physical therapy (core stabilization and lumbar flexibility), from 2026-05-15 to 2026-07-10, totaling 20 visits, as documented in the physical therapy discharge note — this exceeds the guideline's stated minimum of six weeks. In addition, I completed a 4-month trial of NSAIDs with inadequate relief, and a corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-14 that provided only 4 weeks of partial relief. Under the guideline's own definition, this constitutes "[l]ack of meaningful improvement after a full course of treatment," which is one of the enumerated ways to establish "[f]ailure of conservative treatment."

3. **Imaging correlating with symptoms:** MRI of the lumbar spine on 2026-05-29 shows an L4-L5 disc extrusion with severe right lateral recess stenosis and compression of the traversing L5 nerve root — findings that directly correlate with my radicular right leg/calf pain and the neurologic deficit on exam, and that would meet the guideline's description of "moderate to severe stenosis consistent with clinical signs/symptoms" and "inter-vertebral disc herniation that correlate exactly with the individual's symptoms/signs."

There is no active infection, no untreated substance use, and my BMI (29) does not present a contraindication noted in the record.

**Requested action**

Based on the above, the documentation in the prior authorization packet does, in fact, demonstrate an adequate and guideline-consistent trial of conservative treatment, along with imaging and exam findings that correlate with my symptoms. I ask that Harvard Pilgrim reverse the denial and approve CPT 63030 as requested by Dr. Okafor.

Enclosed with this appeal are:
- Physical therapy discharge note (2026-05-15 to 2026-07-10, 20 visits)
- Records of NSAID trial and corticosteroid injection (2026-05-14)
- MRI lumbar spine report dated 2026-05-29
- Office/exam notes documenting provocative testing and neurologic deficit
- [Letter of medical necessity from Dr. Okafor, if not already on file]
- [Any additional records not listed above]

Please confirm receipt of this appeal and provide written notice of the outcome. If this appeal is not resolved in my favor, I understand I may be entitled to request an independent external review through the Maine Bureau of Insurance. I would appreciate a copy of the specific clinical review criteria/guideline version actually applied to my case, as noted above, to ensure this appeal is evaluated against the correct standard.

Thank you for your prompt attention to this matter. Please contact me at [phone number] or [email address] if additional information is needed.

Sincerely,

Morgan Alvarez
Member ID: W375849485

cc: Dr. Okafor, MD [practice name/address/fax, if available]

*Note on sourcing: The policy language quoted above was retrieved directly from the published Evolent Clinical Guideline 1766 for Lumbar Spine Surgery text. I have not been able to independently confirm that this exact guideline version (as opposed to a different revision or an internal Harvard Pilgrim medical policy) is the one that was applied to my specific August 2026 determination, and I am requesting that confirmation as part of this appeal.
